blocks.text: These terms and conditions (the **Terms**) govern your use of the Liberq website, the Liberq platform and every ordering app, web ordering page and AI waiter powered by Liberq. Please read them carefully. By using any of our services, creating an account, placing an order, subscribing or joining one of our programmes, you agree to these Terms.
These Terms are made up of:

items: **Part A – General terms**, which apply to everyone;
**Part B – Merchant terms**, which apply to restaurants, takeaways and other food businesses that subscribe to Liberq;
**Part C – Partner programme terms**, which apply to marketers and sales partners who introduce merchants to us;
**Part D – Customer terms**, which apply to people who order food through an app or web ordering page powered by Liberq; and
**Part E – Beta testing terms**, which apply to people who test pre-release versions of our apps.

blocks.text: If there is a conflict between Part A and another Part, the more specific Part applies to the extent of the conflict.
Part A – General terms

1.2 You can contact us by email at [hello@liberq.app](mailto:hello@liberq.app) or by phone on +44 7909 865259.
2. Definitions

**Merchant** means a food business that subscribes to the Platform;
**Merchant App** means an ordering app or web ordering page built on the Platform and published under a Merchant's brand;
**Customer** means a person who uses a Merchant App to browse a menu or place an order;
**Partner** means a person accepted onto our partner programme under Part C;
**AI Waiter** means the conversational ordering assistant available in Merchant Apps; and
**Services** means the website, the Platform, Merchant Apps and every other service we provide.

Part B – Merchant terms
10. The subscription

10.1 These Merchant terms, together with your order form or online sign-up (the **Order**), form the agreement between Liberq and the Merchant (the **Merchant Agreement**). The Merchant Agreement starts when we accept your Order.
10.2 You confirm that you are entering into the Merchant Agreement for business purposes and that the person accepting it has authority to bind the Merchant.

10.3 Subject to payment of the fees, we grant you a non-exclusive, non-transferable right for the term of the Merchant Agreement to use the Platform and to make your Merchant App available to Customers.
11. Plans and features
11.1 The features, AI Waiter conversation allowances and prices of each plan (currently Launch, Starter, Growth and Pro) are as described on our website or in your Order at the time you subscribe.

11.2 AI Waiter conversation allowances are monthly and do not roll over. If you regularly exceed your allowance, we may ask you to move to a more suitable plan. We will not charge for additional usage without your agreement.
11.3 We may improve, change or withdraw features from time to time. We will not materially reduce the core functionality of your plan during a paid billing period.
12. Set-up and launch
12.1 To build your Merchant App you will provide your logo, brand colours, menu, prices, allergen information and any other content we reasonably request (**Merchant Content**).

12.2 We will use reasonable endeavours to launch your Merchant App within the timescale indicated at sign-up. Launch dates depend on you providing complete Merchant Content promptly and on review by Apple and Google, which we do not control.

12.3 Your Merchant App will be published through the developer account agreed at onboarding. Apple's and Google's terms and policies apply to app store publication, and either may reject or remove an app at its discretion.
13. Fees and payment
13.1 You will pay the one-off set-up fee and the subscription fees for your plan. On the Launch plan you will also pay the per-order fee, capped each month at the amount stated for that plan.
13.2 Subscription fees are billed monthly in advance, or annually in advance where you choose annual billing. Per-order fees are billed monthly in arrears.
13.3 All fees are exclusive of VAT, which you will pay at the applicable rate.
13.4 The set-up fee becomes non-refundable once we have started building your Merchant App.

13.5 Invoices are payable within **14 days** of the invoice date, unless paid automatically by card or direct debit. If you pay late we may charge interest under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 and, after giving you at least 7 days' notice, suspend your Merchant App until payment is received.
13.6 We may change our prices by giving at least **30 days' notice**. Price changes do not apply to an annual period you have already paid for.

13.7 **No order commission.** We do not take a commission on the value of your orders. Card payments are processed by our payment provider (currently Stripe) under its own terms, and its processing fees are charged to you by that provider. Delivery charges from third-party delivery providers are also separate.
14. Your responsibilities
You are responsible for:

items: the accuracy and lawfulness of your Merchant Content, including menu descriptions, prices, offers and images;
providing complete and accurate **allergen and dietary information** for every item, in line with food information law (including the Food Information Regulations 2014), and keeping it up to date;
preparing, packaging and supplying food safely and in line with food hygiene law, including holding any required food business registration;
holding every licence you need, including any licence to sell alcohol, and carrying out age verification for age-restricted products;
fulfilling, cancelling and refunding Customer orders and handling Customer complaints about your food and service;
complying with consumer protection law in your dealings with Customers; and
keeping your dashboard login details secure and ensuring your staff use the Platform properly.

blocks.text: 15. The AI Waiter
15.1 The AI Waiter uses artificial intelligence to understand Customer requests and suggest items from your menu. It relies on the Merchant Content you provide.

15.2 AI-generated responses can be incomplete or inaccurate. The AI Waiter is a helpful ordering aid, **not** a source of allergy, nutritional or medical advice. Merchant Apps tell Customers to check allergen information with you before ordering.
15.3 You must not configure or prompt the AI Waiter to make claims about your food that you cannot substantiate.
16. Payments, delivery and third-party services
16.1 Customer payments are made to you through your account with our payment provider. We are not a party to the sale of food between you and your Customers and do not hold your funds.
16.2 If you use a third-party delivery provider (such as Stuart or Uber Direct), its own terms apply and it is responsible for its couriers' performance.
16.3 We are not responsible for the acts, omissions or availability of third-party services, though we will help you resolve integration issues within the Platform.

17.1 You keep ownership of your brand and Merchant Content. You grant us a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use, copy, adapt and display your Merchant Content to provide the Services, to build and operate your Merchant App and, with your prior approval, to showcase your Merchant App in our marketing.
17.2 You confirm that you have the right to grant this licence and that your Merchant Content does not infringe anyone's rights.
17.3 We own the Platform and all improvements to it, including improvements suggested by you.
18. Data protection

18.1 For personal data about your Customers processed through your Merchant App, **you are the controller and we are your processor**. We will process that data only on your documented instructions and in accordance with Article 28 of the UK GDPR, including by:

items: keeping it confidential and secure using appropriate technical and organisational measures;

helping you respond to Customer rights requests and meet your security, breach-notification and impact-assessment obligations;
notifying you without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach; and
deleting or returning the data at the end of the Merchant Agreement, unless the law requires us to keep it.

blocks.text: 18.2 You must have a privacy notice for your Customers and a lawful basis for any marketing you send them.
18.3 We are the controller of personal data about you and your staff that we use to manage the Merchant Agreement, as described in our Privacy Policy.
19. Availability and support

19.1 We will use reasonable endeavours to keep the Platform available and to fix faults promptly. Planned maintenance will be scheduled, where possible, outside peak trading hours, with advance notice.
19.2 We do not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free service. Support is available by email at [hello@liberq.app](mailto:hello@liberq.app).
20. Term, cancellation and termination
20.1 Monthly subscriptions continue month to month until cancelled. You may cancel by giving at least **30 days' written notice**, ending at the end of a billing month.

20.2 Annual subscriptions run for 12 months and renew for a further 12 months unless either party gives at least 30 days' notice before the renewal date. Annual fees are not refundable for an unused part of the year, except where we terminate for convenience or where the law requires otherwise.

20.3 Either party may terminate the Merchant Agreement immediately by written notice if the other commits a material breach that is not remedied within 14 days of being notified, or becomes insolvent.
20.4 We may suspend a Merchant App immediately if it is being used unlawfully, presents a food-safety or security risk, or puts the Platform or other merchants at risk.

20.5 On termination, your Merchant App will be withdrawn from app stores and web ordering. For **30 days** after termination you may request an export of your menu data and order history, after which we will delete it in line with clause 18.
21. Liability
21.1 Subject to clause 7.1, we are not liable for any loss of profits, revenue, business, goodwill or anticipated savings, or for any indirect or consequential loss.
21.2 Subject to clause 7.1, our total liability under or in connection with the Merchant Agreement in any 12-month period is limited to the total fees you paid to us in that period.

21.3 You will indemnify us against claims by Customers or third parties arising from your food, your Merchant Content, your breach of food safety, allergen, licensing or consumer law, or your breach of the Merchant Agreement.
22. Confidentiality

Each party will keep the other's confidential information secret and use it only to perform the Merchant Agreement. This does not apply to information that is public, already known, independently developed, or required to be disclosed by law.
Part C – Partner programme terms
23. Joining the programme
23.1 The partner programme is free to join. Applicants must be at least 18, and we may accept or decline any application at our discretion.

23.2 Partners are independent contractors. Nothing in these Terms creates an employment, agency, partnership or joint-venture relationship. You have no authority to make promises or enter into contracts on our behalf.
24. Qualifying merchants

24.1 A **Qualifying Merchant** is a food business that (a) you introduce to us in the way we specify, (b) was not already a customer or in active discussions with us, (c) signs a Merchant Agreement within 90 days of your introduction, and (d) pays its set-up fee and first monthly subscription.
24.2 If more than one Partner introduces the same merchant, the first introduction we record will qualify. Our records are final, acting reasonably.
25. What you earn
25.1 **Go-live bonus:** 25% of the set-up fee actually paid by the Qualifying Merchant, payable once the Qualifying Merchant's first monthly subscription has been paid.

25.2 **Commission:** 20% of the subscription fees actually received from the Qualifying Merchant, excluding VAT, for the first 6 months of its subscription. Commission for months 1–3 is paid after month 3, and commission for months 4–6 is paid after month 6, provided the Qualifying Merchant is still subscribed at that point.
25.3 For Merchants on the Launch plan, commission is calculated on the fees actually paid, including per-order fees, for the relevant months.
25.4 For annual subscriptions, commission is calculated as if the Qualifying Merchant had paid monthly at the equivalent monthly rate for the first 6 months.

25.5 No commission is payable on fees that are refunded, credited, unpaid or reversed. If a payment we have made to you relates to fees later refunded or reversed, or to a referral that breaches these Terms, we may deduct that amount from future payments or ask you to repay it.
26. Payment and tax
26.1 We pay earnings by bank transfer within 30 days of the end of the month in which they become payable.
26.2 You are responsible for your own tax and National Insurance and, if you are VAT registered, for providing a valid VAT invoice. We may operate a self-billing arrangement with your agreement.
27. How you must promote Liberq
You must:

items: describe Liberq accurately, using our current materials, and not make claims about savings, earnings or features that we have not approved;
make clear that examples of savings are illustrative;

comply with marketing and data protection law, including the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 — in particular, you must not send unsolicited marketing emails or texts without the required consent; and
not bid on our brand name in paid search advertising, register domains or social accounts using our name, or misrepresent your relationship with us.

blocks.text: 28. Changes and termination
28.1 We may change the commission rates or programme rules on 30 days' notice. Changes do not affect earnings for Qualifying Merchants introduced before the change takes effect.

28.2 Either party may end your participation at any time by written notice. We will pay earnings that have already become payable, unless we end your participation because of your serious breach of these Terms or fraud.
28.3 Subject to clause 7.1, our total liability to you under the partner programme is limited to the earnings payable to you in the preceding 12 months.
Part D – Customer terms
29. Who you are buying from

29.1 When you order through a Merchant App, **your contract for food and drink is with the Merchant** (the restaurant or takeaway), not with Liberq. The Merchant is responsible for the food, its preparation, its description and price, delivery or collection arrangements, and any refunds.
29.2 Liberq provides the technology that lets you browse the menu, chat with the AI Waiter, place and pay for your order and track it.
30. Your account
30.1 You may need an account to place orders. You must give accurate details, keep your password secure and tell us if you think your account has been misused.

30.2 You must be at least 13 to create an account, and at least 18 to order alcohol or any other age-restricted product. The Merchant or courier may ask for proof of age and refuse to hand over age-restricted items.
31. Orders and payment
31.1 Your order is an offer to buy from the Merchant. A contract is formed when the Merchant accepts your order, which is confirmed in the app.

31.2 Prices, delivery charges and any service charges are set by the Merchant and shown before you pay. Payments are processed securely by our payment provider; we do not store your full card details.
31.3 The Merchant may decline or cancel an order, for example if an item is unavailable. If an order is cancelled after you have paid, you will be refunded.
32. Allergies and dietary needs
32.1 Allergen information is provided by the Merchant. **If you have a food allergy or intolerance, please contact the Merchant before ordering** to confirm that a dish is suitable.

32.2 The AI Waiter can help you find dishes that match your preferences, but its responses are generated automatically and may be incomplete or wrong. Do not rely on the AI Waiter as your only source of allergy, nutritional or medical information.
33. Cancellations, refunds and complaints

33.1 Because food is made to order and is perishable, the 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 does not apply once the Merchant has begun preparing your order.

33.2 If there is a problem with your food — for example it is missing, incorrect or not of satisfactory quality — please contact the Merchant through the app as soon as possible. You have rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which the Merchant must honour.
33.3 If you have a problem with the app itself, contact us at [hello@liberq.app](mailto:hello@liberq.app).
34. Using the AI Waiter
34.1 You can talk to or type to the AI Waiter. Please do not share sensitive personal information it does not need — dietary needs and allergies are enough to help it find suitable dishes.
34.2 You must not use the AI Waiter to generate content unrelated to ordering, or try to make it produce harmful, unlawful or misleading content.
35. Our liability to Customers

35.1 If we fail to comply with these Terms, we are responsible for loss or damage you suffer that is a foreseeable result of our breach or our failure to use reasonable care and skill. We are not responsible for loss or damage that is not foreseeable.
35.2 We provide the Services for domestic and private use. We are not liable to you for any loss of profit, loss of business, business interruption or loss of business opportunity.
35.3 The Merchant, not Liberq, is responsible for the food and drink you buy.
